title: Open subgroups and finite etale covers
statement: Let $Y$ be a connected scheme [def-weil-connected-scheme] with a geometric point $\bar y$, and put $G=\pi_1(Y,\bar y)$ [def-galois-fibre-functor]. Finite etale covers and their geometric fibres are as in [def-galois-categories]. The assignment sending a nonempty connected finite etale cover $P\to Y$ to the conjugacy class of $\operatorname{Stab}_G(p)$, for any $p\in |P_{\bar y}|$, is a well-defined bijection between isomorphism classes of such covers and conjugacy classes of open subgroups of $G$. More precisely, isomorphism classes of pointed nonempty connected finite etale covers $(P,p)$ of $Y$, with $p\in |P_{\bar y}|$ and isomorphisms required to carry the marked geometric-fibre point to the marked point, correspond bijectively to individual open subgroups by $(P,p)\mapsto\operatorname{Stab}_G(p)$. In both forms the degree of $P\to Y$ (its constant finite locally free rank [def-pc-finite-locally-free]) equals $[G:\operatorname{Stab}_G(p)]$.

proof.text: Use the existing finite-etale Galois-category instances (Basic.preGaloisCategory, fiberFunctor and galoisCategory). Mathlib PreGaloisCategory.functorToAction is full and faithful, and functorToContAction is an equivalence. A connected cover is a connected categorical object by isConnected_of_connectedSpace; Mathlib FiberFunctor.isPretransitive_of_isConnected makes its fibre transitive. This uses the already proved finite-etale interface directly and does not need the FLC/base-change clauses of thm-galois-fundamental.

Conversely, suppose the fibre of P is nonempty and transitive. A noninitial monomorphism i:Z→P has a fibre point z. Given p in the fibre of P, move i(z) to p by an automorphism of the fibre functor; naturality gives a preimage of p. The fibre map is injective because i is mono, so it is bijective; conservativity makes i an isomorphism. Thus P is a connected object, and the already proved connectedSpace_of_isConnected in FundamentalGroup.Connected makes its underlying scheme connected. This replaces the clopen-to-two-copies detour.

The fibre has the discrete topology and the evaluation action is continuous, so Mathlib stabilizer_isOpen gives openness. The existing Mathlib index_stabilizer_of_transitive gives index equal to Nat.card of the fibre.

For an open subgroup H of G=Aut(fiber s), H.quotient_finite_of_isOpen makes G/H finite and QuotientGroup.discreteTopology gives its discrete topology. Its quotient action is continuous and transitive. Transfer it along an equivalence from a ULift of a finite ordinal, so the resulting finite continuous action has universe u even though G is larger. Essential surjectivity of Mathlib functorToContAction realizes this action by a cover P. Transfer the point 1H and transitivity through the action isomorphism; step 2 makes P connected and MulAction.stabilizer_quotient identifies its marked stabilizer with H.

For equal stabilizers, choose a transporter k(x) with k(x)p=x for each fibre point x, and define f(x)=k(x)q. The equality ap=bp iff aq=bq follows from equality of stabilizers applied to b⁻¹a. It proves independence, equivariance and injectivity; transitivity on the second fibre proves surjectivity. Fullness of functorToAction lifts f to a cover map; fibre conservativity makes it an isomorphism preserving the points. Conversely naturality and the injectivity of a fibre isomorphism preserve stabilizers. Finally transitivity expresses an arbitrary isomorphism image of p as gq; h fixes gq iff g⁻¹hg fixes q, which proves both directions of the conjugacy criterion from the pointed criterion.

A finite etale map f is finite locally free. The pullback universal property gives an explicit equivalence from (fiber s).obj P to the Ω-points of the affine geometric pullback h=pullback.snd f s. Compose with the existing, proved Scheme.Hom.overHomEquivAlgHom; the proved Algebra.Etale.natCard_algHom_eq_finrank computes the cardinality as h.finrankΓ. These library lemmas apply to arbitrary etale algebras and affine schemes, with no group-scheme hypothesis. Scheme.Hom.fiberDegree_of_isPullback and fiberDegree_eq_finrankΓ identify this with f.fiberDegree at the image of a point of Spec Ω. finiteLocallyFree_fiberDimension_isLocallyConstant is constant on the connected base, so every fibre degree equals this number. Step 3 identifies the number with the stabilizer index.

lean.statement: theorem connected_cover_open_subgroups {Y : Scheme.{u}} [ConnectedSpace Y] {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Y) : (∀ (P : Y.FiniteEtale), ConnectedSpace P.obj.left → ∀ p : (fiber s).obj P, IsOpen (MulAction.stabilizer (Aut (fiber s)) p : Set (Aut (fiber s))) ∧ P.obj.hom.IsFiniteLocallyFreeOfDegree (MulAction.stabilizer (Aut (fiber s)) p).index) ∧ (∀ H : Subgroup (Aut (fiber s)), IsOpen (H : Set (Aut (fiber s))) → ∃ (P : Y.FiniteEtale), ConnectedSpace P.obj.left ∧ ∃ p : (fiber s).obj P, MulAction.stabilizer (Aut (fiber s)) p = H) ∧ (∀ (P Q : Y.FiniteEtale), ConnectedSpace P.obj.left → ConnectedSpace Q.obj.left → ∀ (p : (fiber s).obj P) (q : (fiber s).obj Q), (∃ e : P ≅ Q, (fiber s).map e.hom p = q) ↔ MulAction.stabilizer (Aut (fiber s)) p = MulAction.stabilizer (Aut (fiber s)) q) ∧ (∀ (P Q : Y.FiniteEtale), ConnectedSpace P.obj.left → ConnectedSpace Q.obj.left → ∀ (p : (fiber s).obj P) (q : (fiber s).obj Q), Nonempty (P ≅ Q) ↔ ∃ g : Aut (fiber s), ∀ h : Aut (fiber s), h ∈ MulAction.stabilizer (Aut (fiber s)) p ↔ g⁻¹ * h * g ∈ MulAction.stabilizer (Aut (fiber s)) q)

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $Y$ be connected with geometric point $\bar y$. Assigning to a
connected finite etale cover $P$ the stabilizer in $\pi_1(Y,\bar y)$ of a
point of $P_{\bar y}$ is a bijection between the isomorphism classes of
connected finite etale covers of $Y$ and the open subgroups of
$\pi_1(Y,\bar y)$, and the degree of $P$ over $Y$ is the index of the
subgroup.

proof.text:
Here $\pi_1=\pi_1(Y,\bar y)=\operatorname{Aut}(F_{\bar y})$ is the group
of [def-galois-fibre-functor] and the covers are the finite etale
covers of [def-galois-object]. Under [thm-galois-fundamental] connected finite etale covers of $Y$
correspond to transitive finite continuous $\pi_1$-sets — the
transitivity being that of [lem-galois-transitive] — i.e. to
$\pi_1/H$ with $H$ open: the stabilizer of a point of $P_{\bar y}$ is
that subgroup, and $\#F_{\bar y}(P)=\#\pi_1/H=[\pi_1:H]$ is the degree. A
morphism of connected covers corresponds to an equivariant map
$\pi_1/H\to\pi_1/H'$, which exists exactly when $H'$ is contained in
$H$ up to conjugacy, so the assignment is bijective on isomorphism
classes.
